title: OTel collector fixture: config must be a readable temp file and the collector always terminated
answers: collector container left running after a failed test
docker collector cannot read config file in tests
how to pass otel collector config to docker in tests
why does the otel_collector fixture yield only log path and port
body:
Invariant: the collector config is written to pytest tmp_path (kept alive for the whole fixture) and bind-mounted read-only at /etc/otelcol/config.yaml; it is chmod 0o644 so the container user can read it.
Enforced in tests/tracing/conftest.py:otel_collector: the yield sits inside try/finally, and the finally block always calls process.terminate(), then wait(timeout=5), then kill() on timeout.
What breaks if skipped: a failed readiness check leaves a docker run process (and container) alive for later tests; a non-world-readable config makes the container fail to start its config load.
Consumers unpack exactly two values: `output_file, port = otel_collector` (log path, OTLP port). Do not reintroduce the process object or stdin writes into the fixture.
applies: Any change to the otel_collector fixture or the tests that consume it in tests/tracing.
says: Tracing test suite leaves orphaned collector containers running in the background after test failures
Collector container fails to start during tracing tests because configuration permissions prevent reading
Ensure background test containers are always terminated when tracing integration tests fail
search: In tests/tracing/conftest.py:otel_collector, the OpenTelemetry collector configuration must be written to a world-readable temporary file and the container process must always be terminated. The config file is created in pytest tmp_path with chmod 0o644, bind-mounted read-only at /etc/otelcol/config.yaml, and cleaned up in a finally block that calls process.terminate() followed by wait(timeout=5) and kill(). Consumers unpack only output_file and port, without reintroducing the process object or writing configuration via stdin.
